text:
incidents-bot: Alert: Elevated p95 latency detected for inference-runtime in eu-west-1 starting ~2033456785. Auto-page target: oncall.

Mike (oncall): saw the page. digging in now. any broad customer impact flagged?

Priya (SRE): We're seeing p95 jump from ~220ms -> ~1.1s over last 8m for requests routed to 'runtime-v3' in eu-west-1. No error rate increase. Traffic volume steady. heatmap shows tail at busy seq len 1024.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): joining. can you paste the short `bt` from the runtime? curious about queueing vs. kernel spikes.

Mike (oncall): output from `runtime-metrics query`:
```
metric: p95_latency
scope: eu-west-1/runtime-v3
values: [220ms, 280ms, 420ms, 780ms, 1.1s]
concurrency: 32 -> 34
queue_depth: increased by ~18
cpu: normal
gpu_util: 92% on pod pool-3
```

Mike (oncall): looks like batch formation is increasing queue depth and GPU util is high. not seeing errors in logs. will try immediate mitigation: enable overflow routing to runtime-v2 (quantized) and bump pool size by 2.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): +1 to overflow routing. runtime-v2 is slightly lower quality but much cheaper and lower latency under these sequences. I'll flip the canary route now. Also pushing small hotfix to reduce max batch size from 64->48 for eu nodes.

Priya (SRE): FYI oncall, please also check prefix/KV cache hit rate. If KV cache is cold for long sequences that could explain it.

Mike (oncall): KV hit rate currently 67% -> dropping to 45% on long sequences. ok doing route change now.

status-bot: Status page draft: "Degradation: Increased inference latency (p95) in EU region, started 2033456785 UTC. We are routing a portion of traffic to a lower-latency model variant and scaling capacity. Customers may notice slower responses for long inputs. No errors or data loss reported. Engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 15 minutes." Do you want to publish?

Eve (Customer Ops): publish minimal advisory. Suggested customer message for high-traffic customers:
"We are investigating increased inference latency for some requests in our EU region. We have applied traffic routing and scaling mitigations. If you rely on strict p95 SLOs, consider pinning to dedicated capacity or using `runtime-v2` model variant as a temporary fallback. We'll update within 15 minutes."

Sam (Support): I'll pre-draft CS internal note: "Impact: intermittent high p95 latency in eu-west-1 affecting general hosted API customers for long-sequence requests. Workaround: set shorter max tokens or use runtime-v2. ETA: 20-30m for recovery after scaling and route change."

Jordan (Eng Runtime): route change applied: `traffic split: runtime-v3=65%, runtime-v2=35%` for eu-west-1 canary. Reduced max batch size applied to eu runtime nodes. Kicking off +2 pods to pool-3.

Mike (oncall): GPU util dropping to ~75% post changes, p95 trending down to 480ms. KV cache warming back up (now 60%). Keeping watch. If p95 stays >500ms we'll continue scaling.

Priya (SRE): Perf note — this aligns with a sequence-length shift in incoming workload. Suggest longer-term: adaptive batch sizing and KV cache prioritization for prefix-heavy workloads. Capture in postmortem.

Eve (Customer Ops): publishing status now with the draft from status-bot. I'll also message the top 10 paying customers via email template. Sam — want me to copy your internal note into the CS tracker?

Sam (Support): yes please. I'll open a private CS thread with affected customers list.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): small telemetry note: saving the `trace_id` for 2033456802-2033456890 window for deeper gpu kernel profiling. Will follow with snapshot.

status-bot: Status update published: "Mitigation applied; partial traffic routing to a lower-latency model and additional capacity launched. p95 reduced from ~1.1s -> ~480ms and trending down. Investigations continue."

Mike (oncall): current p95 ~360ms, queue_depth back to normal. I plan to close the page once stable for 15m. leaving monitoring runbook active.

Priya (SRE): agree. when closing please include action items: 1) postmortem owner 2) short-term config tweaks 3) follow-up for autoscaler thresholds.

Eve (Customer Ops): Customer email sent to impacted accounts. template used:
"We're reaching out to let you know we're investigating increased latency in our EU inference service. We've applied routing and scaling mitigations; you may see improved latency now. If you observed production errors or need a dedicated channel, reply to this message and we'll escalate."

Mike (oncall): marking recovery window: 2033456920 -> 2033457005 stable. Closing page if stable until 2033457065.

Jordan (Eng Runtime): saved heap and kernel traces; will attach to the postmortem doc.

Sam (Support): internal CS note posted in tracker and Slack private channel, plus list of impacted customers.

status-bot: Incident closed on status page: "Service performance restored to within expected ranges. We'll publish a follow-up postmortem in 48 hours with root cause and action items."

Mike (oncall): thanks all. Postmortem owner: Jordan. I'll add timeline and runbook gaps. Priya, please own autoscaler threshold follow-up.

Priya (SRE): ack. I'll open a ticket with proposed adaptive-pacing and cache-warming heuristics. ETA for RFC: 2 weeks.

Eve (Customer Ops): follow-up comms template for customers after postmortem ready:
"Thanks for your patience. We experienced temporary increased p95 latency in EU region caused by a workload shift toward longer sequences. Mitigations were applied (traffic routing to runtime-v2, batch sizing reduction, and capacity scale-up). No data loss. We will implement preventive measures; postmortem attached." :thumbsup:

Mike (oncall): closing thread. If anything regresses, re-page oncall. :wave:
